note: Gap-slerm backlog. Kept OUT of wubuwizard/docs/GOALS-1000.json so the exactly-1000 / 16-domain invariant survives. Every vendored mechanism in third_party/tiny MUST have exactly one goal here, and a goal may only be marked DONE when its gate target exists and passes.
policy: Every small gap filled is a slerm goal. A vendored file is a SCAFFOLD and a test oracle; it never ships in the product. The end state is own C11 for every mechanism.

goals.title: Slerm the miniz mechanism: own C11 deflate/ZIP decode (RFC 1951 + APPNOTE 4.3.7)
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_inflate.c implements deflate/ZIP decode (RFC 1951 + APPNOTE 4.3.7) from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_inflate asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and miniz is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_inflate prints '34 passed, 0 failed'. 25 streams produced by Python zlib at levels 0/1/6/9 across empty, 1-byte, 900-byte text, 4 KB repetitive, 1 KB random and 32 KB zeros, in both wrappers (zlib header+Adler-32 and raw DEFLATE as a ZIP entry holds); plus 9 refusal/proof cases: truncation, bad Adler-32, flipped payload byte, dst too small, block type 3, preset dictionary, null arguments, the RFC 1950 adler32 vector, and a hand-built stored block whose first bytes are ALSO a valid zlib header. Independently proven against a real ZIP entry (312 -> 2071 bytes, exact) and a real PNG (8,258 IDAT -> 9,264 scanline bytes, exact). miniz is no longer needed for decoding and is not linked anywhere.)]

goals.title: Slerm the stb_image mechanism: own C11 PNG + BMP decode (pixmap)
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_pixmap.c decodes PNG (8-bit, colour types 0/2/3/6, filters 0-4, non-interlaced) and BMP (24/32-bit BI_RGB) with no upstream code in the product; test_wubu_pixmap compares real pixel bytes against files produced by an independent generator and asserts five named refusals. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_pixmap prints '18 passed, 0 failed'. 12 decode cases (PNG grey across all five filter types plus a mixed-filter image, RGB with filters 0 and 4, RGBA with filter 1, palette expansion, BMP 24 and 32) each compared byte-for-byte on pixels, and 6 refusal cases (bad CRC, truncation, unsupported bit depth, scratch too small, pixel buffer too small, non-image input). Mutation-proven: disabling the Paeth predictor leaves 3 failures. STAGE 1 ONLY: JPEG and GIF are refused by name, not decoded.] [naming 2026-11-27: this landed first as src/runtime/wubu_image.c, which OVERWROTE the existing container-image header of the same name and broke the OCI/pkgmgr build. Restored from git and renamed to wubu_pixmap (a decoded raster), because wubu_image already means a container image.]

goals.title: Slerm the stb_truetype mechanism: own C11 TrueType rasterising
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_truetype.c implements TrueType rasterising from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_truetype asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and stb_truetype is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line.

goals.title: Slerm the stb_vorbis mechanism: own C11 Vorbis decode
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_vorbis.c implements Vorbis decode from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_vorbis asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and stb_vorbis is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line.

goals.title: Slerm the dr_wav mechanism: own C11 RIFF/WAVE read+write
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_wav.c decodes RIFF/WAVE (PCM 8/16/24/32-bit and IEEE float 32/64) to interleaved floats, refuses ADPCM/mu-law/A-law by name, and encodes PCM16; test_wubu_wav compares every sample against fixtures written by Python's wave module and hand-built containers at the sign/scaling edges. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_wav prints '11 passed, 0 failed'. Fixtures: 16-bit mono and 8-bit stereo written by Python's own wave module (foreign writer), 24/32-bit and float32 hand-built with payload bytes at 0x800000, INT32_MIN and +/-0.999; encode->decode round trip within one 16-bit quantum; refusals for mu-law, a non-WAVE RIFF (AVI) and an undersized buffer. Mutation: dropping the 24-bit sign shift leaves a failure.]

goals.title: Slerm the dr_mp3 mechanism: own C11 MPEG-1 Layer III decode
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_mp3.c implements MPEG-1 Layer III decode from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_mp3 asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and dr_mp3 is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line.

goals.title: Slerm the monocypher mechanism, stage 1: own BLAKE2b (RFC 7693)
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_blake2b.c implements BLAKE2b (RFC 7693) as a streaming hash with keyed mode, and test_wubu_blake2b compares digests against Python hashlib for six vectors plus every chunking of a 1 KB input, refusing illegal output and key lengths. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_blake2b prints '14 passed, 0 failed'. Vectors from hashlib: empty, 'abc' (also the RFC 7693 appendix value), keyed 'abc' with a 32-byte key, 256-byte and 1024-byte patterns, and a 32-byte digest. Streaming in 1/7/128/129/1000/1024-byte chunks equals the one-shot digest. The gate found a real defect: RFC 7693 caps the key at 64 bytes, and accepting 65..128 reached memcpy() with the caller's pointer -- a null dereference when the key was NULL. Fixed to fall back to unkeyed and to refuse a NULL key with a non-zero length. STAGE 1 ONLY: X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 are the separate goal below.]

goals.title: Slerm the lz4 mechanism: own C11 LZ4 block compression
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_lz4.c implements LZ4 block compression from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_lz4 asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and lz4 is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line.

goals.title: Slerm the cJSON mechanism: own C11 JSON parse/emit
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_json.c is the single JSON reader (no second copy) and is strict where the previous lenient one was not: decoded escapes including surrogate pairs, real doubles, duplicate keys refused, ':' and ',' required, depth bounded at 32, leading zeros refused, and no trailing data; test_wubu_json asserts 41 cases including every one of those refusals. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_json prints '41 passed, 0 failed'; mutation (disabling the duplicate-key check) leaves 1 failure. This REPLACED the existing 161-line lenient parser rather than adding a second one: same header, same token type. Fixing it exposed a real writer bug -- src/gui/wubu_settings_io.c emitted a trailing comma whenever icon_layout_count was 0, so settings.conf was invalid JSON that only the lenient reader accepted; the writer is fixed and make test_settings is 37/37. Dependent gates re-run green: test_settings, test_wubu_aur, test_json_fuzz.]

goals.title: Slerm the utf8 mechanism: own C11 UTF-8 iteration/case/width
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_utf8.c implements UTF-8 iteration/case/width from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_utf8 asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and utf8 is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_utf8 prints '24 passed, 0 failed'. Decode/encode round-trip for ASCII, 2/3/4-byte sequences including U+10FFFF; seven INVALID encodings refused (overlong 2- and 3-byte, surrogate, beyond U+10FFFF, stray continuation, truncated 2- and 4-byte); whole-buffer validity; counting that never lies low; width (combining 0, CJK/emoji 2, control 0); fit that never splits a character or exceeds a cell budget; case mapping for ASCII, Latin-1, Latin Ext-A, Greek (incl. final sigma) and Cyrillic. Mutation-proven: disabling the overlong check leaves 2 failures.)]

goals.title: Slerm the tinyexpr mechanism: own C11 expression parsing and evaluation
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_expr.c implements expression parsing and evaluation from the specification with no upstream code compiled into the product; test_wubu_expr asserts round-trip and fail-closed behaviour against streams generated by an independent oracle, and tinyexpr is absent from mk/objects.mk and every link line. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_expr prints '28 passed, 0 failed'. 16 value cases with oracles computed in Python at double precision (precedence, right-associative ^, unary minus, float/exponent literals, 11 functions, vars pi/e), 2 variable-binding cases, and 10 refusal cases (div0, mod0, sqrt(-1), log(-1), unknown name, trailing token, empty, unbalanced paren, wrong arity). No vendored expression code is compiled: tinyexpr was never installed.)]

goals.title: Password policy on account creation: rules with reasons, not a boolean
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_pwpolicy.c decides whether a password may create an account, answering with a named reason (length in CHARACTERS, class mix, a common-password list, the user name and its reverse, dominance and long runs), and test_wubu_pwpolicy pins every decision in both directions. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_pwpolicy prints '25 passed, 0 failed'. The gate caught three real policy bugs in the first draft: the common-password list was checked AFTER the character-class rule, so 'Password123' was refused for the wrong reason; and the padding/run rule only rejected strings that were ENTIRELY one character or ENTIRELY a run, so 'aaaaaaaaaA1' and 'abcdefghijK1' both passed. It now refuses a character covering >=70% of the string or a six-long straight run, and checks the common list before classes because the advice matters. Mutation: disabling the dominance rule leaves a failure. Acceptance cases are tested too, including a 10-character CJK passphrase counted in CHARACTERS not bytes.]

goals.title: Password reset after re-authentication
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_account.c implements password reset after re-authentication with a behaviour gate that fails on the pre-fix tree; the gate is wired into the default tier and asserts a refusal path, not only the happy path.

goals.title: .wua/WET web view control over WuBuWeb
goals.criterion: src/gui/shell/wubu_webview.c implements .wua/wet web view control over wubuweb with a behaviour gate that fails on the pre-fix tree; the gate is wired into the default tier and asserts a refusal path, not only the happy path.

goals.title: WubuClip stage A: a clipboard of typed representations with a preference rule
goals.criterion: src/bridge/wubu_clip.c holds several MIME-typed representations of one clipboard item, replaces rather than duplicates a repeated type, answers 'first type I can accept' from a caller-supplied preference list, refuses malformed MIME types and NULL data with a length, and reports its capacity by name; test_wubu_clip pins every one of those decisions. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_clip prints '26 passed, 0 failed'. Cases: three representations of one item, preference order for a rich app (html first), a terminal (plain only) and an image request; an unsatisfiable request returns nothing rather than a wrong type; replacing a type keeps one entry and bumps the generation; a MIME parameter ('text/plain;charset=utf-8') is refused as a type; capacity refused by name; clear bumps the generation so 'cleared' differs from 'never set'. Mutation: ignoring the preference list leaves failures. STAGE A ONLY: the host transport (bridge.c's single string and a Wayland data device) is the goal below, so 'clipboard has types' is not claimed yet.]

goals.title: .wua manifest promote read by all four app surfaces
goals.criterion: src/apps/app_manifest.c implements .wua manifest promote read by all four app surfaces with a behaviour gate that fails on the pre-fix tree; the gate is wired into the default tier and asserts a refusal path, not only the happy path.

goals.title: Agent verdict log: tamper-evident record of what the agent did (/n/log/agent)
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_agent_log.c writes an append-only verdict log whose every record commits to the previous one with BLAKE2b, resumes a verified chain instead of restarting it, and refuses to append to a broken log; test_wubu_agent_log asserts append/verify/resume plus edit, deletion, truncation and a SELF-CONSISTENT forgery. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_agent_log prints '24 passed, 0 failed'. The gate caught a hole in its own first draft: an edited record fails on its own hash and a deleted one on the sequence gap, so neither proved the CHAIN. The added case forges a middle record and recomputes its hash exactly as an attacker with the format would; only the next record's commitment to it can catch that, and with chaining disabled the case fails while the rest pass. Fields containing a '|' or newline are refused rather than escaped.]

goals.title: Own bitmap font path: our .fnt equivalent, no upstream font shipped
goals.oracle: third_party/tiny/cozette/cozette.fnt (glyph shapes may be measured; the FORMAT and loader are ours)
goals.criterion: src/gui/wubu_font_bitmap.c loads OUR bitmap font container (header + glyph table) and renders at integer scales with no upstream file in the product; test_wubu_font_bitmap asserts every ASCII glyph box is non-empty and that a truncated container is refused.

goals.title: Own action icons: a hand-drawn master per UI action
goals.oracle: third_party/tiny/feather-icons (shape reference only, never baked into the product)
goals.criterion: src/gui/icons/wubu_action_icons.c resolves every action id the shell asks for to an own master in assets/icons/actions/, and test_wubu_action_icons fails when any action id the shell requests has no master.

goals.title: GIF87a/89a decode (stage 2A of the image gap): own LZW, palette, interlace, transparency
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_gif.c decodes the first frame of a GIF87a/89a file -- LZW over the sub-block chain, global or local palette, four-pass interlacing, transparency -- into RGBA with no size cap and no allocation, and test_wubu_gif compares pixels against fixtures from an independent GIF writer while refusing truncation, non-GIF input, a corrupt code stream and an undersized buffer. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_gif prints '8 passed, 0 failed', and a Pillow-written GIF decodes pixel-for-pixel identical to Pillow's own RGBA read. Mutation: ignoring the interlace passes leaves a failure. Animation timing and frame compositing are NOT implemented and are the separate goal below.]

goals.title: Stage 2 of the crypto gap: own ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439)
goals.oracle: RFC 7748 (X25519) and RFC 8439 (ChaCha20-Poly1305) test vectors, plus Python cryptography as a second reader
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_aead.c implements ChaCha20, Poly1305 and the RFC 8439 AEAD seal/open in C11 with one Poly1305 context shared by the one-shot API and the MAC, and test_wubu_aead compares tags and ciphertexts against Python cryptography while refusing tampered ct/tag/AAD/nonce WITHOUT writing plaintext. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_aead prints '41 passed, 0 failed'. 4 Poly1305 vectors including the RFC 8439 section 2.5.2 value (c57a74fb...), and 6 AEAD vectors (empty, AAD-only, one block, two blocks, 1000 bytes, 16+16) each checked for seal ciphertext+tag, round-trip open, flipped ciphertext byte refused with the output buffer PROVEN untouched, flipped tag, flipped AAD, wrong nonce, and an undersized buffer refused before any work. Mutation: dropping AAD from the MAC leaves 8 failures. X25519 is the separate goal below, so 'crypto' never reads as finished while key agreement is missing.]

goals.title: Stage 3 of the crypto gap: X25519 key agreement (RFC 7748)
goals.oracle: RFC 7748 section 5.2 vectors, the iterated 1/1000 test, and Python cryptography as a second reader
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_x25519.c computes X25519 (RFC 7748) with a masked Montgomery ladder over five 51-bit limbs, clamps the scalar internally, and refuses an all-zero (low-order) result while zeroing the output; test_wubu_x25519 asserts both section 5.2 key pairs, the published shared secret, four independent random pairs, the iterated 1 and 1000 vectors, and the refusals. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_x25519 prints '12 passed, 0 failed'. Oracles: RFC 7748 section 5.2 alice/bob public keys and the shared secret 4a5d9d5b..., four random pairs from Python cryptography, the iterated 1 (422c8e7a...) and 1000 (684cf59b...) vectors, low-order point refused with the output proven zeroed, null arguments, and a check that clamping is internal (raw 0xFF scalar agrees with its clamped form). Mutation: disabling the conditional swap leaves 10 failures. This closes the crypto channel: BLAKE2b, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and X25519 are all our own C11 now.]

goals.title: JPEG baseline decode (stage A of the image family)
goals.oracle: Pillow and an independent JPEG decoder as second readers; progressive and 4:2:0/4:4:4 corpora
goals.criterion: src/runtime/wubu_jpeg.c decodes baseline sequential JPEG -- any of the legal chroma subsamplings, 1 or 3 components, restart intervals -- and REFUSES progressive, arithmetic, 12-bit and CMYK by name; test_wubu_jpeg compares against Pillow-encoded files within a stated tolerance (mean <= 2.0, worst <= 8) plus a structural check that the red square is red and in place. [verified 2026-11-27: make test_wubu_jpeg prints '18 passed, 0 failed'. Measured against Pillow: 4:2:0 mean |diff| 0.34 / worst 2, 4:4:4 0.04 / 2, greyscale 0.01 / 1. Three real bugs caught by the gate: nearest-neighbour chroma upsampling cost 7.94 mean and 92 worst (bilinear triangle filter, as libjpeg, took it to 0.34 / 2 and the tolerance was then TIGHTENED to 2.0 / 8 so a regression fails); a file truncated mid-scan decoded successfully because the bit reader padded with zeros -- now refused as SHORT; and an oversized image was allocated before the cap was consulted. Mutation: nearest upsampling restored leaves 2 failures. STAGE A ONLY: progressive JPEG and GIF animation remain the goal below.]

goals.title: WubuClip stage B: wire typed clipboard into the bridge and the data device
goals.criterion: src/bridge/bridge.c carries the WubuClip model across the host boundary so a copy in one app is pastable in another with its type intact, and test_wubu_clip_bridge proves a round trip for text/plain, text/html and image/png plus a fallback when the consumer accepts only plain text.

goals.title: JPEG progressive decode and GIF animation (image family stage B)
goals.criterion: wubu_jpeg_decode accepts SOF2 progressive files (spectral selection and successive approximation across multiple scans) and wubu_gif decodes every frame with delays, disposal methods and looping into a frame list; test_wubu_jpeg_progressive and test_wubu_gif_anim compare each scan's pixels and each frame against Pillow.

goals.title: Slerm the TrueType glyph rasteriser: outlines, quadratic curves, hinting-free scanline fill
goals.oracle: Pillow ImageFont.truetype (FreeType) rendering the same glyph at the same ppem; per-glyph pixel comparison with a stated tolerance
goals.criterion: wubu_truetype loads a .ttf (head/maxp/cmap/hhea/hmtx/loca/glyf/simple+composite), maps Unicode via cmap format 4 and 12, decomposes quadratic Beziers, and fills an 8-bit coverage bitmap per glyph. test_wubu_truetype compares rendered glyphs against Pillow/FreeType at 12/13/16/20 ppem: identical advance widths, coverage mask mean error below the pinned tolerance, and a mutation that drops one Bezier segment must fail the comparison. Gate must also prove the rasteriser is reachable from the shipped hosted binary, not only from its own test.
why: Visual parity with Win11 is impossible with a 13 px bitmap cell; Selawik (SIL OFL 1.1) is the metric-compatible Segoe UI replacement but needs an outline rasteriser to be drawn.
font_family in settings has no consumer today: a setting that changes nothing is the same defect class as a theme that claims a radius it does not draw.
goals.progress: stages 1-2 DONE: sfnt/cmap/metrics; glyf simple+composite outlines; quadratic flattening; scanline coverage (test_wubu_truetype, 18 checks, mutation-proven). stage 3a DONE: Selawik 1.01 vendored digest-pinned with acceptance probe test_selawik_font (8 checks; found the short-hmtx defect). stage 3b DONE: glyph cache keyed (gid, ppem, subpixel quarter) over a shelf-packed atlas, hit byte-identical to a fresh raster, mutation-proven (test_wubu_text_cache, 27 checks). stage 3c OPEN: call the cache from the shell's text path with the Microsoft epx type ramp, replacing the 13px compiled cell.

goals.title: Flip the baked text cells to Selawik and adapt the control-panel layouts
goals.oracle: tools/font_bake.py (FreeType via Pillow) + test_applet_layout painted-bounds checks
goals.criterion: Both cells baked from Selawik (regular + bold, fallback DejaVu for uncovered codepoints), AND test_applet_layout green at 6px MIN_PAD on every panel at 800x560/1024x768/1600x900. Measured with the Selawik cells in place: all 39 panel/size combinations change bounds; content tops move by 0, +2 or +4 px depending on the panel; the five failures (firmware, mirror, account, limits, signin) gain exactly +3 px at the bottom -- the same 3 px the line height loses (19 -> 16) -- and clamp at H-4 = 896 against the 6 px rule. Widths differ by 1 px on 53 of 188 codepoints; ascent 15 -> 13. Gate: test_wubu_font_text pins the baked table (224 glyphs, 36 legitimately blank, 12385 coverage bytes, ascent+descent==line height, no printable hole) and test_applet_layout keeps the 6px rule on every panel.
goals.next: measure each failing panel's content height, take 6px out of padding/spacing, re-run.
goals.why: The shipped text cells are derived from Microsoft's Segoe UI, which is not redistributable; Selawik is the OFL metric-compatible substitute, but its metrics move every string, so the swap needs measured layout adaptation rather than a table swap.
goals.progress: DONE: both cells baked from Selawik (regular + DejaVu fallback for the 12 codepoints Selawik lacks; bold vendored 44,068 B, digest-pinned). The blocker was not the face but a real padding defect it exposed: five control panels anchored their footer to h - line_h - WUBU_SPACE_XS, i.e. a 4px bottom pad against the 6px MIN_PAD rule, and Segoe's taller line height (19 vs 16) had been hiding the violation by lifting the footer 3px. Discriminated by experiment: anchoring firmware's footer 3px higher (literal 19) restored y[16..893] and passed; the pad, not the glyphs, was at fault. Fixed by using WUBU_SPACE_SM (8) at all five sites, which satisfies 6px for any face. test_applet_layout 276/0 with both the Selawik and the old cells, test_font_aa 0 failed, standards/ratchet/docs/owned-surface green.

goals.replaces: per-size baked coverage (one 13px table was the only drawable size)
goals.title: Runtime text face: draw any ppem through our own engine
goals.oracle: Pillow/FreeType whole-string composition: getlength for advance, L-mode mask sum for ink, 8 strings x 13/20/28 px
goals.criterion: A face opened from a path or from memory draws UTF-8 at any ppem into an ARGB8888 target, composed advance within 2px of FreeType's fractional sum, ink ratio 0.89..1.05, second pass rasterises nothing, malformed UTF-8 refused.
goals.why: The baked cell can only draw one size, so the shell cannot have a type ramp (Win11 uses 12/14/18/20/28/40 epx). The parser, outline decoder, rasteriser and cache existed but nothing composed a string.
goals.progress: DONE: wubu_text_face.{h,c} (open_file owns its bytes, open_memory borrows), pen accumulates in quarter pixels -- rounding each glyph to whole pixels drifts 5.5px over 20 glyphs and fails the gate (mutation recorded) -- glyph cache keyed by subpixel bucket, draw returns the advance (not the pen). Measured: worst advance delta 1.9px on a 20-glyph run, 0.9px on a 44-character line; ink 0.91..1.02 over 24 string/size rows; 99 checks pass. Wiring it into the shell's display sizes is SLERM-2030.

goals.replaces: 13px-only headings (every title in the shell drawn at the caption step)
goals.title: Display-size headings through our own engine, with a baked fallback
goals.oracle: rendered pixels: ink rows measured from the draw output, plus the SLERM-2029 Pillow string oracle for advance
goals.criterion: A heading drawn at the ramp's 20 epx step sits inside its band and is centred within 2px, and returns -1 when no face is loaded so the caller falls back to the baked cell.
goals.why: Win11's caption step is 12 epx, so the 13px cell is right for captions and body text. The visual deficit is hierarchy: every heading in the shell was also 13px, so nothing read as a title.
goals.progress: DONE: shell_text owns one face, draws 20 epx headings, returns -1 as the fallback signal (bare metal keeps the baked cell). Control Panel's 'Settings' is the first surface using it; hosted loads the vendored Selawik at startup with WUBU_FACE as an override. Centring uses the string's MEASURED ink box, not hhea extents: em-centring left 'Settings' 6px low (gap above 9, below 3), after the fix 6/6. Mutations: em-ish centring fails 2 checks; returning 0 instead of -1 fails 1. 14 checks pass. Extended to every settings page: thirteen applet pages each drew their own title by scaling the 13px baked cell 2x (antialiasing enlarged, not outlines), now one owner in cp_page_title() drawing at the Title step (28px) with the scaled cell as fallback. test_applet_layout runs all 117 panel/size checks twice -- with the face and with WUBU_LAYOUT_FACE=none -- so the layout is proven to fit with the taller titles, not only with them missing. shell_text 17 checks; mutation (Title step == heading step) fails 'the title is larger than the heading'.

goals.replaces: bilinear resample of the 13px cell for magnified (accessibility) text
goals.title: Magnified text re-rasterises outlines instead of upscaling a bitmap
goals.oracle: rendered pixels: soft-edge share of ink vs the bilinear upscale, plus the 26px Pillow row for the same word
goals.criterion: At text scale 2 the scaled path asks a registered face renderer for ppem 26 and draws from it; with no renderer registered the output is byte-identical to the previous bilinear resample.
goals.why: Microsoft's text-scaling guidance states DirectWrite/GDI do not natively scale text and apps must render at the larger size; resampling a 13px cell enlarges its antialiasing, so accessibility text was the blurriest text in the shell.
goals.progress: DONE: vbe holds an optional VbeFaceTextFn (kernel keeps no GUI/filesystem dependency); shell_text_vbe registers an adapter that converts box-top to baseline by the face's own ascent. Measured on 'Settings' at 200%: soft edge pixels are 368/753 (49%) crisp vs 931/1202 (78%) bilinear -- ink mass alone cannot tell them apart (1.01 ratio), which is why the gate measures the soft share. Mutations: an adapter that always declines fails 3 checks; detaching reproduces the old bytes exactly. 13 checks.

goals.replaces: fixed-geometry control panel layout that assumes 100% text scale
goals.title: Control panel layout survives the accessibility text scale
goals.oracle: test_applet_layout painted-bounds checks run with vbe_set_text_scale(2)
goals.criterion: All 117 panel/size checks pass at text scale 2 as well as 1, with 6px MIN_PAD; no panel clips its content when text is doubled.
goals.why: Microsoft's text-scaling docs illustrate the failure mode as 'text scaling with text clipping'. Measured here: 20 of 276 checks fail at scale 2 -- the shell does not survive its own accessibility setting.
goals.progress: DONE: 200% text went from 20 failures to 0. Three defects, and only one was obvious: (1) cp_row drew values unclipped past the row edge -> cp_draw_text_fit (vbe_ellipsize); (2) 15 prose sentences were drawn as single lines up to 1222px wide on an 800px panel -> wrapped; (3) cp_text_wrapped itself wrapped by max_w/(8*scale) CHARACTERS, assuming a fixed 8px glyph -- the AA face is not 8px and a re-rasterised 26px glyph is ~13px, so wrapping was present and panels still overflowed.
